**Guaranteed departure dates in 2026:** 4–14 February, 5–15 March, 6–16 April, 1–11 May, 10–20 October and 1–11 November.

**Maximum group size:** 16 people.

An English-speaking guide leads the mainland Ecuador programme. Tours in the Galápagos Islands are also led by an English-speaking guide.

## Trip highlights

The first few days focus on Quito and the Andes. See the capital's historic centre, the Basilica del Voto Nacional, Plaza San Francisco and El Panecillo, as well as two sites associated with the equator: Mitad del Mundo and the Intiñan Museum.

The route then takes you to a rose plantation, the Quilotoa crater lake and Baños. In Baños, the itinerary includes a city tour, the Agoyán, Manto de la Novia and Pailón del Diablo waterfalls, and the well-known Swing at the End of the World.

After Baños, the route climbs into the highlands. Visit the Chimborazo reserve, see vicuñas and a mountain refuge, and explore the Ingapirca archaeological complex. Then continue to Cuenca, Cajas National Park and a cacao hacienda on the way to Guayaquil.

The final four days take you to the Galápagos. On Santa Cruz, see giant tortoises and lava tunnels. The visit to Bartolomé includes a climb to a viewpoint, beach time and snorkelling. Another boat trip visits either North Seymour and Bachas or South Plaza and Punta Carrión. The exact option is confirmed after booking.

## How the itinerary works

Guaranteed departures are for small groups of up to 16 people. English-speaking assistance is provided on the mainland, and an English-speaking guide leads the excursions in the Galápagos Islands. An English-speaking driver takes you from Quito airport to your hotel on arrival. A Spanish-speaking escort accompanies the final transfer from the hotel to the airport in the Galápagos.

Altitude varies considerably along the route. Quito sits at around 2,800 m. Baños lies lower, at about 1,826 m, near the 5,016 m Tungurahua volcano. The route then climbs back into the highlands towards Chimborazo, Ecuador's highest mountain, at over 6,000 m. Conditions in the Galápagos are quite different, with a maritime climate, island highlands and coastal terrain.

Accommodation changes along the route. The itinerary uses the 4-star Finlandia in Quito, the 3-star La Floresta in Baños, the 4-star Casa Real in Riobamba, the 4-star El Dorado in Cuenca, the 4-star Palace in Guayaquil and the 3-star Fiesta in Puerto Ayora on Santa Cruz.

Meals vary by day. Dinner with the guide is included on the first evening. A packed lunch is provided on the long day visiting Chimborazo and Ingapirca. Lunch is included at the cacao hacienda. Breakfast and lunch may be served aboard the yacht on Galápagos boat trips.

A few restrictions affect the programme. The rose plantation cannot be visited on weekends or public holidays. Ingapirca is open from Wednesday to Sunday. On other days, you can see the ruins from outside. At Quilotoa, kayaks and mules cost extra, and local mule services operate until around 15:00. The island visited on day 10 is confirmed after booking.

Galápagos charges are also paid separately: the flight to the islands, admission to the national park and the INGALA transit control card. These are excluded from the base tour price and are listed separately below.

## Hotels and meals along the route

The group spends two nights at the 4-star Finlandia in Quito. Dinner is included on day 1 and breakfast on day 2. After Quilotoa, stay at the 3-star La Floresta in Baños, then at the 4-star Casa Real in Riobamba. After visiting Chimborazo and Ingapirca, spend two nights at the 4-star El Dorado in Cuenca. Stay at the 4-star Palace in Guayaquil, followed by three nights at the 3-star Fiesta on Santa Cruz.

Breakfast is included daily on the mainland except where meals are specified separately. A packed lunch is also included on the day you visit Chimborazo, and lunch is included on the day you visit Cajas and the cacao hacienda. Breakfast and lunch are included on Santa Cruz on days 8–10. On day 11, breakfast is included before departure.
